title: Streaming output fractionation during capacity surge — action plan and follow-ups
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a capacity surge on 2026-03-09 we observed widespread partial streaming outputs and client disconnects for hosted API customers. Symptoms included fragmented token chunks, mid-stream socket disconnects that left clients with incomplete tokens, and elevated 502/504 rates from proxy tiers. This ticket captures the incident follow-ups, root cause analysis synopsis, mitigation already applied, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence.

Impact:
- Several production customers experienced truncated streaming responses or repeated reconnects during a two-hour window.
- Latency SLOs breached for streaming endpoints in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
- Increased unit cost due to repeated retries and replays.

Scope and goals:
1) Finish immediate hardening to prevent truncated streams on capacity spikes.
2) Implement observability for token-level continuity across retries.
3) Remediate configuration regressions in autoscaler and batching logic.
4) Track follow-ups and owners to closure by due_date.
timeline: 2026-03-09T01:12Z - First customer alarm: mobile app reporting truncated streams
2026-03-09T01:35Z - Identified surge in request concurrency from several tenants and a simultaneous autoscaler downscale event in us-west-2
2026-03-09T01:50Z - Applied mitigation: temporarily raised autoscaler min-pools and pinned model variants to low-latency kernels
2026-03-09T03:10Z - Metrics returned to baseline; customers reported reduced failures
2026-03-10 - Post-incident triage meeting; created this ticket for follow-ups
root_cause_summary: Primary cause was an interaction between a recent autoscaler tuning change (reduced headroom thresholds) and a regression in continuous-batching heuristics that extended batching windows under high concurrency. That combination increased tail latency; backpressure signals from the runtime were delayed and occasionally lost in the request pipeline due to an edge case in the token-commit race (race between socket close handling and KV cache flush), resulting in partial token delivery and disconnects.
detection: Detected via elevated 5xx rates, streaming continuity alerts, and customer reports. The Console streaming continuity dashboard showed bursty token-gap increases aligned with autoscaler events. Packet-level traces showed socket resets during KV commit operations.
mitigation_performed: Raised autoscaler min-pools in affected regions to restore headroom (manual override)
Pinned model variants to previously verified low-latency kernel path for affected tenants
Rolled back recent batching heuristic commit (reverted PR #1284) to restore previous batch window behavior
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha: Triage complete. Root cause points to autoscaler + batching interaction. Need concrete follow-ups across runtime, autoscaler, and proxy layers.
2026-03-11 - Diego: Confirmed token-commit race reproducible in integration harness. Created test harness case 'stream-frag/regress-2026-03'
2026-03-11 - Priya (SRE): Added short-term alert for token-gap rate > 5/min to trigger autoscaler headroom protection
2026-03-12 - Kara (Product): Notify top affected customers and prepare support FAQ for truncated streams
action_items: A1: Add token-continuity metric and alerting (owner: Priya SRE) — instrument at runtime and proxy. Due: 2026-03-17
A2: Harden backpressure signal pathway so signals are delivered before socket close handling (owner: Diego) — code change + unit tests. Due: 2026-03-20
A3: Re-evaluate autoscaler headroom defaults and add safety override when streaming continuity alert fires (owner: Ben, Autoscaler) — config + integration test. Due: 2026-03-18
A4: Add integration test in CI that reproduces batching window expansion under burst load (owner: Sandeep, Runtime) — test + flakiness guard. Due: 2026-03-22
A5: End-to-end chaos test simulating simultaneous downscale + high-concurrency streaming (owner: SRE team) — runbook + weekly job. Due: 2026-03-24
A6: Postmortem doc and external customer summary (owner: Kara, Support/Product) — publish and notify customers. Due: 2026-03-16
next_steps: Complete A1 and A2 as top priority (both P0). Once implemented, run canary for 72 hours in us-west-2.
Coordinate with sales/support to identify top 10 customers impacted and offer credit/assistance where appropriate.
Schedule deep-dive on continuous-batching heuristics to consider moving to bounded windows rather than heuristic-driven expansion.
